therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: nucleoside analog incorporation leading to DNA chain termination
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: prevention of tumor cell proliferation and recurrence
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients with superficial bladder cancer undergoing transurethral resection

subgroup_findings: High risk (G3) patients showed numerically better outcomes with gemcitabine: 66.7% vs 42.4% recurrence-free at 12 months
Recurrent disease patients showed numerically better outcomes with gemcitabine: 72.2% vs 58.9% recurrence-free at 12 months
Patients without BCG showed numerically better outcomes with gemcitabine: 79.9% vs 74.5% recurrence-free at 12 months
results.dose_information: 2000 mg intravesicular instillation x 1 immediately post transurethral resection
